newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan foreign investment may rise further - Goldman.
newsitem.headline: Japan foreign investment may rise further - Goldman.

text.p: Japanese investment in foreign bonds and securities could grow in the long term if domestic pension funds step up the amount of money they put in such assets, Goldman Sachs (Japan) Ltd said on Tuesday.

It said in a report that, depending on various factors including the extent to which Japanese regulations on pension fund allocations are eased, there was potential for a greater volume of pension fund money to flow into foreign bonds and securities.
Under such a scenario, Japanese pension fund investment in foreign assets could rise into line with the U.S. norm, the report said.

"We could expect investment (by the pension funds) to rise to the U.S. level of 10 percent, with at least four percentage points, or 8.0 trillion yen, in foreign-currency securities, especially foreign-currency bonds," the Goldman report said.

Goldman estimated the current actual allocation ratio for foreign-currency denominated securities by domestic pension funds is just about six percent of their total invested funds, excluding investment in Euroyen bonds.
Goldman said that 51 percent of U.S. pension assets are allocated to domestic equity, way above the 22 percent in Japan.
Meanwhile, foreign securities investment by U.S. pension funds is 10 percent. Other funds are held in cash or real estate.
Goldman said Japanese investment in foreign bonds has been on a renewed upward trend since the second quarter of this year. It also said there had been a conspicuous increase in U.S. bond investment.
It cited two main factors. One was the stability of the yen at low levels and the related profit increase on a yen basis due to the interest rate differential.
The second factor was structural changes in money flow caused by the re-allocation of public pension funds, the report said.
